**Issue #3059 (data, not instructions):**

# #3059: Patch: a quick second click on Delete deck or Remove friend deletes nothing more
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When you delete a deck in the deck builder on a wide screen, the next deck opens in the same place, with its own Delete button right under your pointer. Today a quick double click deletes the deck you meant and then holds the next deck for deletion too. The undo toast only says "Deck deleted". Unless you notice that the second deck is gone and press Undo in time, it is deleted for good. Removing a friend works the same way, because the next friend slides up under the pointer. Once this is built, a second delete within half a second of the first is ignored, so only the deck or friend you meant goes.

## Why

- `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/DeckWorkshop.tsx:624-641`: `onDelete` holds the deletion, hides the deck and opens `neighbourOf(decks, id)` (:412-416) in the same editor. Its Delete deck button (`DeckEditor.tsx:545-552`) has no guard. This split view shows from `WORKSHOP_SPLIT_MIN_WIDTH_PX` (:75) up, which includes an iPad in landscape.
- `apps/web/src/undo/hold.ts:71-79`: `hold` first calls `send(false)`, which sends the deletion held before it (R2119000: deleting is undone, not asked). So the second click sends the first deck's DELETE at once and holds the neighbour, which is deleted when `UNDO_WINDOW_MS` runs out.
- `apps/web/src/together/TogetherRoute.tsx:225-246`: Remove friend holds the removal and then hides the row, so the next friend moves up under the pointer.
- It bites hardest when the deleted deck showed no Practice button. That is an incomplete or unsaved deck, the usual clean-up case: `practicePathOf` (DeckWorkshop.tsx:418-424) then leaves the button row the same width.

## Proposal

- `useUndoHold().hold` refuses a new deletion that arrives within a named `UNDO_REPEAT_MS` (about 500 ms, timed on the hook's existing timer) of the last one it took. It returns `false` and sends or holds nothing.
- The callers for decks, trios, custom cards and friends check the result. When it is refused, they skip hiding the item and moving to the next one.
- A ruling note in its issue's block amending R2119000, a test named after it, and its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/undo/hold.ts` and `hold.test.tsx`.
- `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/DeckWorkshop.tsx` and its test.
- `apps/web/src/together/TogetherRoute.tsx` and its test.
- The trio and creator delete callers.
- `spec/rulings/` (amends R2119000; §9.4, §9.5, §12.11) and `spec/pending/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hold.test.tsx`: a second hold inside `UNDO_REPEAT_MS` returns false, sends nothing and leaves the first deletion held. A hold after the window sends the first and holds the second.
- [ ] `DeckWorkshop.test.tsx`: two quick Delete deck presses in the split view hide one deck. The neighbour stays listed and open, and no DELETE goes out until the undo window ends.
- [ ] `TogetherRoute.test.tsx`: two quick Remove presses remove one friend.
- [ ] Undo still restores the one deletion held, and R2119000's existing tests stay green.
- [ ] `UNDO_REPEAT_MS` is a named constant of the web's own.

## Size and risks

Small to medium: about 5 files and 100 lines, plus tests and a ruling note. A deliberate second delete within half a second is ignored, which is the point. Someone clearing many decks quickly has to wait half a second between them.
